cards.text: Isaiah son of Amoz is a prophet with a message about Judah and Jerusalem (Isaiah 2:1). He's just said to stop trusting in man, who has only breath in his nostrils (Isaiah 2:22). Now he says behold: the Lord GOD of Hosts is about to remove both supply and support from Jerusalem and Judah.

cards.question: The Lord GOD of Hosts is about to take away Jerusalem's supply. What's on that list?

answers.text: The whole supply of food and water
All the gold in the treasury

cards.question: Along with food and water, who else will the Lord remove from Jerusalem and Judah?

cards.text: Here's who will go: the mighty man, the warrior, the judge, the prophet, the soothsayer, the elder, the commander of fifty, the dignitary, the counselor, the cunning magician and the clever enchanter. Friend, that's not a few people, that's the WHOLE org chart.

cards.question: With all those leaders removed, the next line says kings from other nations will be put in charge of Jerusalem and Judah.

cards.text: Then comes this line: "I will make mere lads their leaders, and children will rule over them."

cards.question: Next, Isaiah tells how the people of Jerusalem and Judah will treat each other. What will they do?

answers.text: They will share what they have
They will stay out of each other's way

cards.text: It will be man against man and neighbor against neighbor. The young will rise up against the old, and the base against the honorable.

Isaiah says a man will seize his own brother inside his father's house: "You have a cloak—you be our leader!" That's like getting promoted to manager because you're the only one in the office who owns a STAPLER.

cards.question: With the food, the water and the leaders all gone, the man will tell his brother to take charge of a heap of ___.
The brother will refuse to become leader of the people.

cards.text: On that day he will cry aloud that he's no healer and has no food or clothing in his house: "Do not make me leader of the people!" First time I've ever heard somebody turn down a job by listing everything he DOESN'T have.
Now Isaiah steps back and looks at the big picture. Jerusalem has stumbled and Judah has fallen, and he tells us why.

cards.question: Why have Jerusalem stumbled and Judah fallen?

answers.text: They spoke and acted against the LORD
Their armies were too small to win
Their walls were not strong enough

cards.text: They've been defying His glorious presence. And Isaiah says the expression on their faces testifies against them.

cards.question: Isaiah says the people of Jerusalem and Judah work hard to hide their sin.

cards.text: Like the city of Sodom (Genesis 19), they flaunt their sin and don't conceal it. Woe to them, Isaiah says, because they have brought disaster upon themselves.

cards.question: Then there's a message to pass along to the righteous. What is it?

answers.text: It will be well with them
They will fall with the rest

cards.question: The righteous will enjoy the fruit of their labor. But woe to the wicked. What will they be repaid with?

cards.text: Then God speaks about the ones in charge of His people.

cards.question: God says His people are being oppressed. Who is doing it?
God tells His people their guides are turning them from their paths.

cards.text: Youths oppress His people and women rule over them, and God says, "O My people, your guides mislead you; they turn you from your paths." You know when your GPS sounds totally sure of itself and steers you straight into a LAKE?
Then the LORD arises to contend. He stands to judge the people.

cards.question: The LORD brings a charge. Who is it against?

answers.text: The elders and leaders of His people
The kings of the nations around Judah
The priests who serve in the temple

cards.text: He tells them they have devoured the vineyard. Then He names what's sitting in their houses.

cards.question: The LORD tells the elders and leaders that the plunder of the ___ is in their houses.

cards.text: "Why do you crush My people and grind the faces of the poor?" declares the Lord GOD of Hosts. And that's where it ends, friend, with that question hanging in the air.
